newsitem.title: MALI: Mali opposition to contest elections.
newsitem.headline: Mali opposition to contest elections.

text.p: Mali's Rally of Patriotic Forces (RFP) opposition alliance, one of two in the West African country, says it will contest this year's national elections even though it rejects a new electoral code.

A statement made public by the six-party alliance on Tuesday expressed reservations about the independence of a national election commission envisaged under the code, but said that it would not complain to the constitutional court.
The alliance "has decided not to challenge the new electoral code but to contest the elections firmly determined to bring about a changeover of political power in Mali," the statement said.

Parliament, where President Alpha Oumar Konare's supporters have a majority, approved the law on January 9. At the same time, it approved the expansion of the national assembly to 147 seats from 116 at present.
No date has been set for the elections which must be held in the first half of 1997.
Mali has two opposition alliances, the second, the Front for Change and Democracy (FCD), also groups six parties. Formed this month, it voted for the new code.

The RFP accuses Konare of not consulting properly on the new code, denouncing the balance of power in the commission. It will have five members each from the ruling party and the opposition plus 10 each from society at large and from public authorities.
Konare, a historian, won a five-year term as president in Mali's successful 1992 democratic transition and is expected to seek a second term.
